ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p137#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p137#2/r1.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p137#2/r1.claim: Al-Khalil and Sibawayh analyze لا جرم as a fixed compound meaning “indeed,” with the following clause raised as its subject.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p137#2/r1.anchor: مذهب الخليل وسيبويه أنهما ركبا من لا وجرم، وبنيا، والمعنى: حق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p137#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p137#2/r2.speaker: الحوفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p137#2/r2.claim: Al-Hawfi treats جرم as negated by لا, nominative as a topic, with أن and its clause as predicate; other grammarians take the construction to mean inevitably or no opposition/prevention.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p137#2/r2.anchor: وقال الحوفي: جرم منفي بلا بمعنى حق، وهو مبني مع لا في موضع رفع بالابتداء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p137#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p137#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p137#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj rejects compounding. Another analysis makes جرم a past verb meaning earned, with an implicit subject and the following clause as object; poems illustrate that root. Al-Nahhas and al-Farraʾ report dialect variants.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p137#2/r3.anchor: وجرم فعل ماض معناه كسب، والفاعل مضمر أي كسب هو، أي: فعلهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p137#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p137#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p137#2/r4.claim: They are the greatest losers because their loss lasts forever, unlike sinners whose punishment ends and gives way to relief.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Those who squandered their abilities on false worship destroyed themselves and will necessarily lose in the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: people who wasted their abilities in this way actually destroyed

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Their imagined gods and the support sought from them are fabricated and useless, leaving people without insight to fail in the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: all their deities will turn out to be baseless since they had actually fabricated them by imputing falsehood to God.

NAHHAS:v2p277/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p277/r1.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه والفراء ومحمد بن يزيد
NAHHAS:v2p277/r1.claim: These grammarians say لا جرم means “truly”; أن is nominative. Al-Khalil says لا marks the statement as a reply, not an opening utterance.
NAHHAS:v2p277/r1.anchor: فقال الخليل وسيبويه جرم بمعنى حق فأن عندهما في موضع رفع وهذا قول الفراء ومحمد بن يزيد

NAHHAS:v2p277/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p277/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v2p277/r2.claim: Abu Ishaq takes لا as denying the supposed benefit and جرم as their deed earning loss, so أن is accusative.
NAHHAS:v2p277/r2.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق لا ههنا نفي لما ظنوا أنه ينفعهم كان المعنى لا ينفعهم ذلك جرم أنهم

NAHHAS:v2p277/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p277/r3.speaker: الكسائي
NAHHAS:v2p277/r3.claim: Al-Kisaʾi explains لا as no denial or prevention of the outcome, and lists forms لا جرم, لا عن ذا جرم, لا أن ذا جرم, and a Fazara form without mīm.
NAHHAS:v2p277/r3.anchor: وقال الكسائي في الإعراب لا صد ولا منع عن أنهم وحكى الكسائي فيها أربع لغات لا جرم ولا عن ذا جرم

NAHHAS:v2p277/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p277/r4.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v2p277/r4.claim: Al-Farra adds dialects لا ذا جرم among Banu Amir and لا جرم with a damma on jīm among some Arabs.
NAHHAS:v2p277/r4.anchor: وحكى الفراء فيه لغتين أخريين قال بنو عامر يقولون لا ذا جرم

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2019#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2019#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2019#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : لا جرم يقول : بلى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p38#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p38#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p38#3/r1.claim: This is a new sentence, and its demonstrative reinforces the preceding one in 11:18; the relative clause describes the known class who lost their own selves by failing to benefit from guidance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p38#3/r1.anchor: استئناف ، واسم الإشارة هنا تأكيد ثان لاسم الإشارة في قوله : { أولئك يعرضون على ربهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p38#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p38#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p38#3/r2.claim: Their invented claims were that idols could intercede or avert hardship; attributing straying to idols mocks their worshipers by picturing the idols losing their way to those who sought help.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p38#3/r2.anchor: ما كانوا يزعمونه من أن الأصنام تشفع لهم وتدفع عنهم الضر عند الشدائد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p38#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p38#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p38#3/r3.claim: The final sentence summarizes the preceding exposure, punishment, refusal to hear warnings, and neglect of monotheistic evidence, all of which establish their loss in the afterlife.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p38#3/r3.anchor: فذلكة ونتيجة للجمل المتقدمة من قوله : { أولئك يعرضون على ربهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p38#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p38#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p38#3/r4.claim: La jarama is an idiom of certainty; Ibn Ashur regards jarama as a fossilized noun meaning inevitably or without alternative, with an omitted preposition governing anna, and the phrase can introduce an oath-like assertion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p38#3/r4.anchor: اسم بمعنى محالة أي لا محالة أو بمعنى بد أي لا بد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p39/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p39/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p39/r1.claim: Calling their harm a loss is a metaphor: like traders they suffered damage while expecting benefit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p39/r1.anchor: وعبر عما لحقهم من الضر بالخسارة استعارة لأنه ضر أصابهم من حيث كانوا يرجون المنفعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p39/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p39/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p39/r2.claim: They are the greatest losers because they combine the forms of misery and punishment scattered among deluded nations, and were miserable precisely where they expected happiness, losing both this world and the next.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p39/r2.anchor: ولأنهم شقوا من حيث كانوا يحسبونه سعادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p39/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p39/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p39/r3.claim: The separating pronoun restricts the judgment rhetorically: they reached the greatest possible loss, as though no one else shared that distinction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p39/r3.anchor: وضمير { هم الأخسرون } ضمير فصل يفيد القصر ، وهو قصر ادعائي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r3.speaker: سيبويه والخليل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r3.claim: They take lā jarama as surely or truly; other grammarians say no doubt, no escape, or necessarily, also attributed to al-Khalil, while al-Zajjaj parses lā as rebuttal and jarama as earning, making their deeds earn them loss.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r3.anchor:
ومعنى لا جرم: حق. هذا مذهب سيبويه والخليل. وقال بعض النحويين:
معناها: لا بد ولا شك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj places an in the accusative after lā as rebuttal, whereas Sibawayh takes it in the nominative; al-Kisaʾi says lā jarama means no turning away or prevention.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r4.anchor: فموضع «أن» على مذهب سيبويه رفع: وموضعها على مذهب الزجاج- نصب. وقال الكسائي معناها لا صد ولا منع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r5.claim: The sense of cutting may underlie jarama, while the earning sense is supported by poetry and by the gloss that a tribe’s jarīma is its earner; Jarir’s line can bear either sense.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r5.anchor: فكأن جرم على هذا من معنى القطع، تقول: جرمت أي قطعت: وهي على منزع الزجاج من الكسب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r6.claim: Lā jarama has dialect variants including lā dhā jarama, lā an dhā jarama, lā ʿan dhā jarama, and lā jar with the mīm dropped through frequent use.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r6.anchor: وفي لا جرم لغات: يقول بعض العرب: لا ذا جرم، وبعضهم: لا أن ذا جرم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r8.claim: Lā jarama has variant forms in Arabic, including lā dhā jarama, lā an dhā jarama, lā ʿan dhā jarama, and a shortened lā jar due to frequent use.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p161#2/r8.anchor: وفي لا جرم لغات: يقول بعض العرب: لا ذا جرم، وبعضهم: لا أن ذا جرم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p91/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p91/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p91/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says lā jarama means “truly.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p91/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس يريد حقا إنهم الأخسرون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p91/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p91/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p91/r2.claim: Al-Farra says lā jarama originally meant “there is no escape or doubt,” then frequent use made it equivalent to “truly”; its root is jarama, to earn sin.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p91/r2.anchor: كانت في الأصل بمنزلة لا بد ولا محالة فجرت على ذلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p91/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p91/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p91/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj construes lā as denying benefit: their deeds do not benefit them; rather, they earned loss in the Hereafter.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p91/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج ومعنى لا جرم لا نفي لما ظنوا أنه ينفعهم كأن المعنى لا ينفعهم ذلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p91/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p91/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p91/r4.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says lā answers unbelievers who think punishment will be diverted, then jarama begins a new clause; jarama either means their unbelief earned punishment or that punishment was made sure, with a poem supporting the latter.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p91/r4.anchor: لا رد على أهل الكفر فيما قدروه من اندفاع الشر عنهم في الآخرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p91/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p91/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p91/r5.claim: The various dialect forms—lā jarama, lā jarama without mīm, lā dhā jarama, and related forms—all mean “certainly.”

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p314#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p314#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p314#2/r2.claim: They are the greatest losers in the afterlife, trading the heights of Paradise and its delights for Hell's depths and punishments, and God's nearness and vision for His anger.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p314#2/r2.anchor: استبدلوا بالدركات عن الدرجات، واعتاضوا عن نعيم الجنان بحميم آن

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p464/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p464/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p464/r2.claim: One interpretation treats لا as an emphatic extra particle, so the phrase means that they truly are the greatest losers in the afterlife; the following line illustrates جرمت as causing or deserving an outcome.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p464/r2.anchor: أن { لا } زائدة دخلت توكيدا , يعني حقا إنهم في الآخرة هم الأخسرون

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p464/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p464/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p464/r3.claim: The line about the thrust that made the Fazāra tribe angry uses جرمت in the sense of causing or making an outcome certain.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p464/r3.anchor:
جرمت فزارة بعدها أن يغضبوا .
أي أحقتهم الطعنة بالغضب

MUQATIL:11:22/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:22/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:22/r1.claim: “La jarama” means certainly: these unbelievers are the greatest losers in the afterlife.
MUQATIL:11:22/r1.anchor: { لا جرم } حقا، { أنهم في الآخرة هم الأخسرون }

NASAFI-FULL:v2p150#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p150#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p150#4/r1.claim: They are the greatest losers in the afterlife because they led others astray and turned away themselves.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p150#4/r1.anchor: ﴿ لا جرم أنهم في الآخرة هم الأخسرون ﴾ بالصد والصدود

NASAFI-FULL:v2p150#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p150#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p150#4/r2.claim: One analysis takes لا as rejecting a preceding claim, جرم as acquired, and the whole as saying their claim earns them loss in the afterlife.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p150#4/r2.anchor: أن لا رد لكلام سابق أى ليس الامر كما زعموا ومعنى جرم كسب

NASAFI-FULL:v2p150#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p150#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p150#4/r3.claim: A second analysis treats لا جرم as a compound meaning truly, with their loss as the subject of what is true.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p150#4/r3.anchor: أن لا جرم كلمتان ركبتا فصار معناهما حقا

NASAFI-FULL:v2p150#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p150#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p150#4/r4.claim: A third analysis understands the expression to mean inevitably.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r2.speaker: الخليل
QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r2.claim: Al-Khalil and Sibawayh take “la jarama” as “certainly,” treating it as one indivisible expression; “anna” is nominative. Al-Farraʾ and Muhammad ibn Yazid also transmit this analysis.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r2.anchor: فقال الخليل وسيبويه: { لا جرم } بمعنى حق

QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r3.speaker: الخليل
QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r3.claim: A second interpretation from al-Khalil and al-Farraʾ makes “la jarama” mean “inevitably” or “without doubt.”
QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r3.anchor: وعن الخليل أيضا أن معناها لا بد ولا محالة

QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r4.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses “la” as denial of the claim that idols benefit, and “jarama” as “earned”: their deed earned loss, with the implied subject omitted and “anna” in the accusative; he supports the root with poetry.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r5.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r5.claim: Al-Kisaʾi says “la jarama” means there is no restraint or prevention from their consequence.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r5.anchor: وقال الكسائي: معنى { لا جرم } لا صد ولا منع

QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r6.claim: Another explanation takes the expression as “no cutting can cut it off,” with the agent suppressed through frequent use; the root means cutting or stripping, as in harvesting dates, shearing wool, and taking meat from bones.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r6.anchor: فحذف الفاعل حين كثر استعماله والجرم القطع

QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r7.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r7.claim: Al-Nahhas reports four forms from al-Kisaʾi—“la jarama,” “wa-la ʿan dha jarama,” and “wa-la anna dha jarama” among them—and notes Fazarans' form without mīm; al-Farraʾ adds “la dha jarama” and a form with ḍamma on jīm.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:21-22/r7.anchor: قال النحاس: وزعم الكسائي أن فيها أربع لغات

RAZI-FULL:v17p166#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p166#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p166#2/r1.claim: They are the greatest losers because the worldly thing they chose over the noble faith cannot endure and will perish.
RAZI-FULL:v17p166#2/r1.anchor: لما أعطى الشريف الرفيع ورضي بالخسيس الوضيع فقد خسر في التجارة

RAZI-FULL:v17p166#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p166#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v17p166#2/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says lā jarama means inevitably or without doubt, and through frequent use came to mean truly.
RAZI-FULL:v17p166#2/r2.anchor: قال الفراء : إنها بمنزلة قولنا لا بد ولا محالة ، ثم كثر استعمالها حتى صارت بمنزلة حقا

RAZI-FULL:v17p166#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p166#2/r3.speaker: النحويون
RAZI-FULL:v17p166#2/r3.claim: One grammatical analysis takes lā as negation and jarama as cutting: nothing can cut off the certainty that they will be the greatest losers.
RAZI-FULL:v17p166#2/r3.anchor: الأول : لا حرف نفي وجزم ، أي قطع ، فإذا قلنا : لا جرم معناه أنه لا قطع قاطع عنهم

RAZI-FULL:v17p166#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p166#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v17p166#2/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says lā denies the benefit they expect and jarama means earning: their conduct earns loss in this life and the next; al-Azharī calls this the best account.
RAZI-FULL:v17p166#2/r4.anchor: الثاني : قال الزجاج إن كلمة { لا } نفي لما ظنوا أنه ينفعهم ، و { جرم } معناه كسب ذلك الفعل

RAZI-FULL:v17p166#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p166#2/r5.speaker: سيبويه والأخفش
RAZI-FULL:v17p166#2/r5.claim: Sībawayh and al-Akhfash take lā as a reply to unbelievers and jarama as “is true”: their unbelief makes punishment and loss rightfully occur; a poetic line uses the root for making a consequence certain.
RAZI-FULL:v17p166#2/r5.anchor: قال سيبويه والأخفش : { لا } رد على أهل الكفر كما ذكرنا وجرم معناه حق وصحح

SAMIN-DURR:11:22/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:22/r1.speaker: الخليل
SAMIN-DURR:11:22/r1.claim: With Sibawayh and most grammarians, لا جرم is a compound of negation and جرم, built like خمسة عشر and meaning حق; the following clause is its subject.
SAMIN-DURR:11:22/r1.anchor: وهو مذهب/ الخليل وسيبويه وجماهير الناس أنهما ركبتا من " لا " النافية و " جرم

SAMIN-DURR:11:22/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:22/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:22/r2.claim: A second analysis treats لا as genus-negating, جرم as its accusative name, the pair as a nominative subject, and the following clause as predicate; sense: certainly.
SAMIN-DURR:11:22/r2.anchor: الوجه الثاني: أن " لا جرم " بمنزلة لا رجل، في كون " لا " نافية للجنس، و " جرم " اسمها مبني

SAMIN-DURR:11:22/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:22/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:22/r3.claim: A third analysis keeps the preceding construction but makes the clause after أن genitive or accusative after an omitted preposition, meaning certainly about their afterlife loss.
SAMIN-DURR:11:22/r3.anchor: الثالث: كالذي قبله إلا أن " أن " وما بعدها في محل نصب أو جر بعد حذف الجار

SAMIN-DURR:11:22/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:22/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:11:22/r4.claim: He takes لا as a reply denying a preceding claim, then reads جرم as a past verb meaning earned, with the implicit deeds as subject and أن-clause as object.
SAMIN-DURR:11:22/r4.anchor: وهذا هو قول أبي إسحاق الزجاج، وعلى هذا فالوقف على قوله: " لا " ثم يبتدأ ب " جرم

SAMIN-DURR:11:22/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:22/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:22/r5.claim: The verb reading is supported by poetry where جرمت means earned, and جريمة can name a group's provider or earner; their actions earned their loss.
SAMIN-DURR:11:22/r5.anchor: جرم فعل ماض معناه كسب، وفاعله مستتر يعود على فعلهم المدلول عليه بسياق الكلام

SAMIN-DURR:11:22/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:22/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:22/r6.claim: A fifth analysis takes جرم to mean cutting or preventing, as a noun under لا; the clause after أن is its predicate or follows an omitted preposition.
SAMIN-DURR:11:22/r6.anchor: الوجه الخامس: أن معناها لا صد ولا منع، وتكون " جرم " بمعنى القطع، تقول: جرمت، أي: قطعت

SAMIN-DURR:11:22#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:22#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:22#2/r1.claim: The expression has variants including different vowels, حذف the final m, and forms beginning ذا or إن; Abu Amr also reports لا جرم with a changed rhyme and لا جر.
SAMIN-DURR:11:22#2/r1.anchor: وفي هذه اللفظة لغات: يقال لا جرم بكسر الجيم، ولا جرم بضمها، ولا جر بحذف الميم

SAMIN-DURR:11:22#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:22#2/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:11:22#2/r2.claim: He explains loss of the m in لا جر by frequent use, paralleling the clipped سو ترى for سوف.
SAMIN-DURR:11:22#2/r2.anchor: وعن أبي عمرو: " لا جرم أن لهم النار " على وزن لا كرم، يعني بضم الراء، ولا جر

SAMIN-DURR:11:22#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:22#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:22#2/r3.claim: هم may be a separator, an emphatic pronoun, or the subject of a new sentence whose predicate is الأخسرون.
SAMIN-DURR:11:22#2/r3.anchor: وقوله: { هم الأخسرون } يجوز أن يكون " هم " فصلا وأن يكون توكيدا، وأن يكون مبتدأ

STUDYQURAN:11:20/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:20/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:11:20/r5.claim: What the disbelievers fabricated, including idols, ideas, and religious beliefs, will ultimately forsake them.
STUDYQURAN:11:20/r5.anchor: one will ultimately be forsaken by what one has fabricated, including false idols, ideas, and religious beliefs

TAB-FULL:v12p373#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p373#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p373#2/r1.claim: They are the greatest losers because they exchanged their homes in Paradise for the homes of the people of Paradise in Hell; al-Tabari also explains لا جرم as an idiom of certainty, literally associated with earning sin and used for inevitability.
TAB-FULL:v12p373#2/r1.anchor: أن معنى قولهم، جرمت: كسبت الذنب، وأجرمته، أن العرب كثر استعمالها إياه في مواضع الأيمان،

TABATABAI:11:22-23/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:22-23/r1.speaker: الفراء
TABATABAI:11:22-23/r1.claim: Al-Farra’ explains “لا جرم” as originally meaning inevitably or without doubt, then developing into an emphatic “truly” or oath-like expression.
TABATABAI:11:22-23/r1.anchor: عن الفراء أن { لا جرم } في الأصل بمعنى لا بد ولا محالة

TABATABAI:11:22-23/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:22-23/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:22-23/r2.claim: Al-Tabataba’i suggests the phrase may derive from “جرم,” cutting: nothing cuts off the conclusion, so the phrase means “truly.”
TABATABAI:11:22-23/r2.anchor: وقد ذكروا أن { جرم } بفتحتين بمعنى القطع فلعلها كانت في الأصل

TABATABAI:11:22-23/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:22-23/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:22-23/r3.claim: They are the greatest losers among the afterlife’s inhabitants because they destroyed themselves through disbelief and have no prospect of salvation while persisting in defiance.
TABATABAI:11:22-23/r3.anchor: فلا مطمع في نجاتهم من النار في الآخرة

TABATABAI:11:22-23/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:22-23/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:22-23/r4.claim: A second possible comparison is with worldly life: they lose both lives, but the afterlife loss is greater because it is everlasting while this life is brief.
TABATABAI:11:22-23/r4.anchor: لكنهم في الآخرة أخسر لكونها دائمة مخلدة

TABATABAI:11:22-23/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:22-23/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:22-23/r5.claim: Deeds intensify through their consequences in the afterlife; the author prefers the first reading because the verse appears to restrict the greatest losers to them there.
TABATABAI:11:22-23/r5.anchor: وأحسن الوجهين أولهما لأن ظاهر الآية حصر الأخسرين فيهم

TABRISI:11:20-22/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:20-22/r7.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:11:20-22/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj parses lā jarama as denying what they thought would benefit them, so their conduct earns the greatest loss; another explanation takes the expression as “necessarily” or “surely,” a decisive assertion that they are the greatest losers in the Hereafter.
TABRISI:11:20-22/r7.anchor: قال الزجاج: لا نفي لما ظنوا أنه ينفعهم كأن المعنى لا ينفعهم ذلك جرم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس؛ أكثر المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384#2/r1.anchor: يقول: حقا إنهم في الآخرة هم الأخسرون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384#2/r2.claim: Lā jarama originally meant “no escape” or “inevitably,” later becoming an emphatic “truly” and sometimes functioning like an oath.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج؛ الأزهري؛ ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj says lā denies the assumed benefit and jarama means earned: their deed earned loss; al-Azharī calls this one of the best explanations, and Ibn al-Anbārī analyzes jarama as a past verb with an implicit subject referring to disbelief.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384#2/r3.anchor: معنى لا جرم: (لا) نفي لما ظنوا أنه ينفعهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384#2/r4.speaker: قوم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384#2/r4.claim: Another explanation treats lā as extra, so their deed earned them regret.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384#2/r4.anchor: (لا) صلة في {لا جرم} والمعنى: كسب لهم عملهم الندامة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384#2/r5.speaker: الأخفش؛ سيبويه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384#2/r5.claim: They take lā as a rejection of the disbelievers’ claim and jarama as “deserved/was certain”; the cited poem uses jaramat to mean that a spear thrust made Ghatafān angry.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384#2/r6.speaker: الفراء؛ أبو العباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384#2/r6.claim: They reject that interpretation, reading Ghatafān as accusative: the wound caused the tribe to become angry.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p384#2/r6.anchor: جرمت فزاره بالنصب، والمعنى جرمتهم الطعنة أن يغضبوا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r1.claim: They are the greatest losers in degree or amount; the definite predicate marks exclusivity, and taking هم as a separator or subject further emphasizes that judgment.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r1.anchor: أي لا أحد أبين أو أكثر حسرانا منهم فأفعل للزيادة إما في الكم أو الكيف

ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r2.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj analyzes لا as negating an omitted clause such as their deed benefiting them and جرم as a past verb meaning earned; the following أن-clause states what the deed earned.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r2.anchor: عن الزجاج أن لا نافية ومنفيها محذوف أي لا ينفعهم فعلهم مثلا و جرم فعل ماض

ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r3.speaker: الشاعر
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r3.claim: An unnamed poet uses جرمت to mean earned or committed, as evidence for the verbal reading of جرم.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r3.anchor: وقال الشاعر : نصبنا رأسه في جذع نخل بما ( جرمت ) يداه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r4.speaker: سيبويه
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r4.claim: Sībawayh takes لا as negative and جرم as the verb حقّ, with the following clause as its subject: their deed cannot benefit them, since their loss is certain.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r4.anchor: ونقل عن سيبويه أن لا نافية حسبما نقل عن الزجاج و جرم فعل ماضي بمعنى حق

ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r5.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r5.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says Sībawayh and al-Khalīl treat the combined لا جرم as meaning certainly; the following clause is its subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r5.anchor: وذكر أبو حيان أن مذهب سيبويه وكذا الخليل أيضا كون مجموع ( لا جرم ) بمعنى حق

ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r6.speaker: الكسائي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r6.claim: Al-Kisāʾī analyzes لا as negative and جرم as its indeclinable noun, with an omitted predicate and a preposition omitted before أن; the idiom means no opposition or prevention.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r6.anchor: وعن الكسائي أن ( لا ) نافية ( وجرم ) إسمها مبني معها على الفتح

ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r7.claim: Another view makes جرم a noun meaning cutting off: their being the greatest losers will never cease, so no contrary state interrupts it.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r7.anchor: وقيل : إن ( جرم ) إسم ( لا ) ومعناه القطع من جرمت الشيء أي قطعته

ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r8.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r8.claim: Al-Sīrāfī transmits from al-Zajjāj that لا جرم first meant not to admit someone into sin, then conventionally came to mean inevitably; al-Farrāʾ is also credited with this explanation.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r8.anchor: ونقل السيرافي عن الزجاج أن ( لا جرم ) في الأصل بمعنى لا يدخلنكم في الجرم

ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r9.claim: Other analyses derive the idiom from جرم as falsehood or earning, yielding the sense truly or certainly; lexicographers record variant forms, some of whose attribution as eloquent Arabic is doubted.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33/r9.anchor: وفي البحر أن ( جرم ) عليه إسم ( لا ) وقيل : إن ( جرم ) بمعنى باطل

ALUSI-FULL:v12p33#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33#2/r1.claim: After completing the account of the disbelievers' conduct and fate, the discourse turns to believers and their good outcome, completing the contrast with the preceding praise of believers.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33#2/r1.anchor: ثم إنه تعالى لما ذكر طريق الكفار وأعمالهم وبين مصيرهم وما لهم شرع في شرح حال أضدادهم

ALUSI-FULL:v12p33#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33#2/r2.claim: Intervening particles between لا and جرم are generally treated as extra; the author tentatively explains a reported form without لا as saying that the fact needs no further assertion.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p33#2/r2.anchor: وحكي بغير لا جرم أنك أنت فعلت ذاك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p169#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p169#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p169#2/r4.claim: Lā jarama means truly; another says rather indeed, and al-Farra glosses it as without doubt. They are the greatest losers in the afterlife even though all are losers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p169#2/r4.anchor: {لا جرم} أي: حقا. وقيل: بلى. وقال الفراء: لا محالة،

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:21-22/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:21-22/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:21-22/r2.claim: Lā jarama means certainly; no one in the afterlife is more plainly or greatly a loser than they are.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:21-22/r2.anchor: لا جرم أنهم فى الآخرة هم الأخسرون } لا أحد أبين وأكثر خسرانا منهم.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r3.claim: “No doubt” identifies these afterlife deniers as the most lost of all, with the repeated pronoun and “they” giving the superlative emphasis.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r3.anchor: ولما كان المقام جديرا بالمبالغة في وصفهم بالخسارة , أعاد الضمير

BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r4.claim: The author defines inability to thwart as being unable to prevent what God wills, doubling as an increase by an equal or larger amount, and capacity as a power by which limbs act.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r4.anchor: والإعجاز : الامتناع من المراد بما لا يمكن معه إيقاعه ؛ والمضاعفة : الزيادة على المقدار بمثله أو أكثر ؛ والاستطاعة : قوة ينطاع بها الجوارح للفعل

BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r5.speaker: الرضي والسفاقسي
BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r5.claim: Al-Radi and al-Saqafsi report several grammatical accounts of “la jarama”: “la” may reject prior speech or be extra because the phrase carries an oath, while Sibawayhi and al-Khalil treat the expression as a compound past verb meaning “it is certain.”
BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r5.anchor: قالالرضي في شرح الحاجبية والبرهان السفاقسي في إعرابه ما حاصله : والغالب بعد { لا جرم } الفتح

BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r6.claim: Other grammarians say “jarama” means “is true,” making it the noun of “la” with “they” as predicate; al-Kisaʾi explains the phrase as “no denial or prevention.”
BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r6.anchor: وقال الكسائي معناها : لا صد ولا منع

BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r7.speaker: الزجاج
BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj treats the phrase as uncombined: “la” denies the claim that idols help, “jarama” means “earned,” and “they” is its object.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r7.anchor: وعن الزجاج أنها غير مركبة , ولا نفي لما قيل من أن لهم أصناما تنفعهم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r8.speaker: الفراهي
BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r8.claim: Al-Farahi derives the expression from an original sense of “inevitably” or “there is no alternative,” with the root referring to cutting, and explains the phrase’s oath-like use.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p516/r8.anchor: وقال الفراهي : كلمة كانت في الأصل بمعنى لا بد ولا محالة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p517/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p517/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p517/r1.claim: The author prefers understanding the root through the recurrent idea of disturbance: in the mind, reflection unsettles an opinion and opens what was closed, while related forms express doubt, confusion, sin, mixture, or separation.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p517/r1.anchor: وقد علم من هذا أن جميع تصاريف المادة تدور على الاضطراب وهو بين في غير العقل

BIQAI-FULL:v3p517/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p517/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p517/r2.claim: On this analysis, “la jarama” means there is no uncertainty or wavering that they will be punished; in context, denying doubt affirms certainty.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p517/r2.anchor: ظهر أن معنى ( لا جرم ) أنهم لا ظن ولا اضطراب في أنهم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p517/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p517/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p517/r3.claim: This also explains Sibawayhi’s gloss “it is true”: “la” negates the opposite of the assertion, so the phrase confirms that their fate is established and every contrary is excluded.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p517/r3.anchor: فكأنه قيل : حق وثبت أنهم كذا وانتفى كل ما يضاده

BIQAI-FULL:v3p517/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p517/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p517/r4.claim: The author treats “la” as an emphatic particle of negation in this expression, comparable to the emphatic force of “innama.”
BIQAI-FULL:v3p517/r4.anchor: فهي نافية لضد ما دخلت عليه , فكأنه قيل : حق وثبت أنهم كذا

BIQAI-FULL:v3p517/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p517/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p517/r5.claim: With fatḥ after “la jarama,” the construction looks to its original “there is no alternative that…” form; kasra reflects its later oath-like force, as in “I swear that you are standing.”
BIQAI-FULL:v3p517/r5.anchor: فمن فتح فللنظر إلى أصل { لا جرم } كما نقول : لا بد أن نفعل كذا

DURR-FULL:v4p413/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p413/r9.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v4p413/r9.claim: Those who lost themselves have cheated or deprived themselves.
DURR-FULL:v4p413/r9.anchor: عن السدي رضي الله عنه {أولئك الذين خسروا أنفسهم} قال: غبنوا أنفسهم

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#3/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#3/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#3/r7.claim: Those in Hūd both obstructed God’s path and misled others, with multiplied punishment, so they are “the greatest losers”; al-Naḥl describes those who themselves preferred worldly life and are losers, without that added harm to others.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#3/r7.anchor: فكان الأولون أخسر من الآخرين فجيء لهم باسم التفضيل
